summary: Registers the audio/mpeg media type so that MPEG-1 and MPEG-2 audio files, such as MP3, can be labeled consistently in email and on the web. Before this, there was no uniform MIME type for them. It is on the standards track.

plainLanguage.summary: Music files need a name tag so computers know what they are. This gives MP3-style sound files one official tag that everyone agrees to use.

questions: what is the mime type for mp3
subtitle: Registers the MIME type for MPEG audio files, including MP3

tldr.problem: MPEG-1 and MPEG-2 audio files (such as MP3) were widely used on the internet and in email, but there was no uniform MIME type to label them consistently.
tldr.mechanism: This RFC registers the media type audio/mpeg to refer to MPEG audio streams. The type covers audio compressed using MPEG-1 or MPEG-2 layer I, II or III compression, with optional metadata like ID3 tags.
tldr.outcome: Email systems, web servers, and applications can now consistently identify MPEG audio files and route them to the correct handlers or players.

today: RFC 3003 is a Proposed Standard that registers the audio/mpeg MIME type for MPEG audio files. It remains published and is universally used to label MP3 and other MPEG audio files in email, on web servers, and in web applications.

sections.title: MPEG Audio Compression
sections.content:
The MPEG-1 and MPEG-2 standards define audio compression methods known as layer I, layer II, and layer III. These compression methods provide low quality loss at high compression ratios, making them popular for distributing audio over the internet.

Compressed MPEG audio is divided into frames, each containing a frame header and compressed audio data. The mime type audio/mpeg defines an elementary byte stream containing MPEG frames according to these standards, possibly interspersed with non-MPEG data (data without proper synchronization or that cannot decompress without error).
sections.plainLanguage: MPEG is a way to compress music so it takes less space but still sounds good. Layer III is what most people know as MP3.

sections.title: Media Type Registration
sections.content:
The media type is registered as audio with subtype mpeg. It has no required parameters and no optional parameters. For transmission over the internet, lower layers handle transmission errors, so audio/mpeg data may include MPEG frames generated without optional cyclic redundancy checks (CRC) for improved audio quality.

MPEG audio data is binary and must be encoded for non-binary transport; Base64 encoding is suitable for email. The file extensions are .mp1, .mp2, and .mp3. MPEG audio is device, platform and vendor neutral and is supported by a wide range of encoders and decoders.
sections.plainLanguage: The type is called audio/mpeg and has no special options. MP3 files are labeled with this type when sent by email or web servers.

sections.title: Security and Metadata Considerations
sections.content: MPEG is a tagged data format, and some tags are available for private use. Arbitrary material could potentially be transferred in the MPEG stream, including executable content. Tagged data containing executable content SHOULD never be sent and MUST not be executed if it is received. Audio/mpeg objects are not signed or encrypted internally; external security mechanisms must be employed to ensure content confidentiality and integrity.
sections.plainLanguage: Someone could hide executable code inside an MP3 file or hide other data in it, so trust the source and never run code from inside an MP3.

references.text: Bradner, S., "Key words for use in RFCs to Indicate Requirement Levels", BCP 14, RFC 2119, March 1997.
